records.title: Photosynthesis
records.licence: TEST FIXTURE (written for unit tests, not a real resource)
records.subject: science
records.text: Photosynthesis is the process by which green plants use sunlight, water and carbon dioxide to make glucose and release oxygen. It takes place mainly in the chloroplasts of leaf cells, which contain the green pigment chlorophyll. The glucose made during photosynthesis is used by the plant for energy and growth.

records.text: ದ್ಯುತಿಸಂಶ್ಲೇಷಣೆ ಎಂಬುದು ಹಸಿರು ಸಸ್ಯಗಳು ಸೂರ್ಯನ ಬೆಳಕು, ನೀರು ಮತ್ತು ಇಂಗಾಲದ ಡೈಆಕ್ಸೈಡ್ ಬಳಸಿ ಆಹಾರವನ್ನು ತಯಾರಿಸುವ ಕ್ರಿಯೆ. ಈ ಕ್ರಿಯೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಆಮ್ಲಜನಕ ಬಿಡುಗಡೆಯಾಗುತ್ತದೆ.

records.title: Water cycle
records.licence: TEST FIXTURE (written for unit tests, not a real resource)
records.subject: science
records.text: The water cycle describes how water moves between the oceans, the atmosphere and the land. Water evaporates from the surface, condenses into clouds and falls back as precipitation such as rain or snow. About 97 percent of Earth's water is in the oceans.

records.title: Vijayanagara Empire
records.licence: TEST FIXTURE (written for unit tests, not a real resource)
records.subject: history
records.text: The Vijayanagara Empire was based in the Deccan Plateau region of South India. It was established in 1336 by the brothers Harihara I and Bukka Raya I. Its capital Vijayanagara, whose ruins surround present-day Hampi, is a World Heritage Site.

records.title: Gravity
records.licence: TEST FIXTURE (written for unit tests, not a real resource)
records.subject: science
records.text: Gravity is the force by which objects with mass attract one another. On Earth, gravity gives weight to physical objects and causes them to fall towards the ground when dropped. The Moon's gravity causes the ocean tides.
